pr_title: Make a number of improvements to the System.Text.Json source generator
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-json, @gregsdennis See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Makes a number of improvements to the System.Text.Json source generator: 1. Ensures that the source generated `JsonTypeInfo` singleton instances are populated via the corresponding `JsonSerializerOptions` cache and are thus preconfigured before they are surfaced to users. The generated metadata properties now look as follows: ```C# internal partial class ClassWithStringValuesContext { private global::System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo? _String; /// /// Defines the source generated JSON serialization contract metadata for a given type. /// public global::System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo String { get => _String ??= (global::System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfo)Options.GetTypeInfo(typeof(global::System.String)); } } ``` 2. Fixes indentation & whitespace issues with generated source code, particularly with contexts not in namespaces. 3. Fix #76829. I've split the relevant changes into separate commits for easier reviewing.

issue_context.title: JSON source generator emits CS0612 warnings if serialized types use [Obsolete]
issue_context.body:
### Description

The JSON source generator should not trigger warnings when used with obsolete types. See [#62076](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62076), which only fixed the bug when the `Obsolete` attribute includes a message.

### Reproduction Steps

Same as [#62076](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/62076), but with `[Obsolete]` instead of `[Obsolete("Use NewValue instead")]`.

### Expected behavior

No warnings.

### Actual behavior

`warning CS0612: 'MyObject.OldValue' is obsolete`

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

_No response_

_No response_

Up for grabs. Same fix as https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/63496, but we're disabling `CS0612` warnings this time.
If we do something for `CS0612`, then we would also need to be able to address obsoletions with custom diagnostic IDs, which can be `SYSLIB` values or user-defined diagnostics.

Even more generally... what if our generated code triggers a diagnostic from a completely different diagnostic, even one that is user-defined and intentionally running over generated code? How would customers suppress any arbitrary diagnostic within our generated code? How would that be configured?

Alternatively we could employ a convention where suppressions active in the partial class are applied to the extra generated code:
```C#
#pragma warning disable CS0618 // gets replicated in all generated instantiations of the partial class

[JsonSerializable(typeof(Foo))]
public partial class MyContext : JsonSerializerContext { }

#pragma warning restore CS0618
```

> This could be added to the existing [`JsonSourceGenerationOptionsAttribute`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.json.serialization.jsonsourcegenerationoptionsattribute?view=net-6.0) via a new property:
> 
> ```cs
> public class JsonSourceGenerationOptionsAttribute
> {
>     public string[]? SuppressedWarnings { get; set; }
> }
> ```
> 
> The source generator reads that attribute at compile time to configure source gen. Usage of the new property would look as follows:
> 
> ```cs
> [JsonSourceGenerationOptions(SuppressedWarnings = new string[] { "CS0612" } )]
> [JsonSerializable(typeof(Foo))]
> public partial class MyContext : JsonSerializerContext { }
> ```

Hi, @eiriktsarpalis !
Is it a final shape of expected API, so it can be implemented in a such way, or should it go through api review process as per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/project/api-review-process.md ?
@Hellevar this needs to go through API review before an implementation PR can be submitted.

review_comments: FWIW, we use IndentedTextWriter for this purpose in the regex generator.
Nice. I think we definitely need to overhaul the formatting tools we're using here.
I see there are a few outstanding issues related to 52218.  Does this address all of them, or are there more still?
It seems to cover a few others as well.The specific concern is rendered obsolete by virtue of the fact that all metadata resolution goes through JsonSerializerOptions for the hot path.
Throwing an exception at configuration time is no longer needed -- this is generally done on serialization by checking the `MetadataSerializationNotSupported` property (set in line 116).
